title: Threshold Majority Queries
summary: Given an integer array nums and an array of queries, for each query, find the element in the specified subarray that appears at least the given threshold times, with the highest frequency, or return -1 if no such element exists.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an array of queries, for each query, find the element in the specified subarray that appears at least the given threshold times, with the highest frequency, or return -1 if no such element exists.
constraints: The array has up to 10,000 values and there are up to 50,000 inclusive range queries.
Choose the highest-frequency value meeting threshold, breaking ties by smaller value.
Return -1 if the maximum frequency is below threshold.
hints: Mo ordering changes only a few boundary elements between neighboring offline queries.
Maintain value frequencies plus lazy min-heaps indexed by frequency.
Add or remove boundary values, clean stale heap entries at the current maximum frequency, then test the threshold.
The highest nonempty frequency bucket is the range mode, and its min-heap root enforces the smallest-value tie rule.
editorial: The highest nonempty frequency bucket is the range mode, and its min-heap root enforces the smallest-value tie rule.

tests.explanation: The answers are one, negative one, and two.
Range modes and the smallest-value tie rule produce 3,2,3,2.
